techniques.name: Classic Boogie Shuffle & Pinky Stretch
techniques.description: Steady swinging shuffle pattern fretting the root note while alternating the 5th, 6th, and minor 7th with the pinky finger

notes: A5 / A6: Open A string + 2nd fret D string (A5), reaching to 4th fret D string with ring/pinky (A6)
D5 / D6: Open D string + 2nd fret G string (D5), reaching to 4th fret G string (D6)
E5 / E6: Open E string + 2nd fret A string (E5), reaching to 4th fret A string (E6)
sequence: Establish the swung eighth-note pulse ('DAH-dum, DAH-dum') at 136 BPM
Keep the index finger barred across fret 2 while bouncing the pinky on fret 4 and 5
Apply light right-hand palm muting near the bridge saddles for percussive chug
tips: Keep your thumb positioned behind the neck centerline to facilitate the pinky fret-4 reach
If the pinky stretch cramps your hand, rotate your fretting wrist slightly forward
Dial in a touch of slapback delay (120ms) for that vintage 1971 Sun Records bounce

beginner.title: Open Chords & Strumming the Progression
steps: Learn open A, D, and E chords cleanly
Practice the 12-bar blues progression in A at 100 BPM
Count the swung eighth notes out loud ('1-and-2-and-3-and-4-and')
beginner.goals: Solid timekeeping through the entire 12-bar form

intermediate.title: The Boogie-Woogie Pinky Stretch
steps: Master the A5 to A6 pinky stretch on strings 5 and 4
Move the exact same grip to D5/D6 and E5/E6
Build stamina at 136 BPM using our Metronome Speed Trainer
intermediate.goals: Fluid boogie shuffle without hand fatigue or dropped beats

advanced.title: Chuck Berry Double-Stops & Lead Fills
steps: Learn Ross Hannaford's sliding double-stops at fret 5 across strings 1 and 2
Incorporate syncopated percussive rake strokes before chord changes
Transcribe the roaring guitar solo with bluesy quarter-tone bends

commonMistakes: Playing straight eighth notes instead of the essential swung shuffle groove
Letting the unused open strings ring out and muddy the boogie riff
Collapsing the left-hand wrist against the neck, making the fret 4 stretch difficult
practiceRoutine: Warm up with 5 minutes of pinky independence exercises on fret 2 and 4
Run the boogie shuffle in A with our Metronome set to 'Shuffle' groove preset
Practice shifting between A5, D5, and E5 without breaking the swing cadence
focusAreas: Fretting-hand wrist relaxation during pinky stretches
Percussive right-hand palm muting for punchy low-end punch
metronomeWork: Select the 'Blues Shuffle' sound preset on our Metronome tool
Start at 105 BPM and practice clean shuffle accents
Work up to the studio tempo of 136 BPM in 5 BPM increments
